## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated current, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating. All other components inspected during this visit are in good condition, but the pump fault prevents normal system operation and treatment.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet, which is normal operation for a Type 2 system. The effluent filter was clean and light soiling was present; it was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP AND ELECTRICAL ASSESSMENT
| Component | Measurement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effluent Pump Amp Draw | 1.6A (nameplate 7.2A) | CRITICAL - No Load |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Good |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | Good |

**Pump Condition - CRITICAL:** The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated full-load amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load -- no fluid is being moved through the discharge line. The most likely causes are a broken or missing impeller, a severed or disconnected discharge line, or a dry-run condition. Running a pump without fluid cooling creates immediate risk of motor overheating and failure. The motor may already be damaged.

## DISPERSAL FIELD ASSESSMENT
The dispersal field surface is dry with no visible breakout or ponding. No deficiencies were observed during the site walk.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. Do not continue operating the system until the pump has been inspected and repaired or replaced. A qualified technician must determine whether the impeller is broken, the discharge line is severed or disconnected, or another mechanical failure has occurred. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is restored to normal operation.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious problem that must be fixed before your system can treat wastewater properly. Do not delay in calling a service technician. The pump motor is at risk of burning out if it continues to run without fluid cooling.

### Solids Management
Your tank solids are at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally as bacteria break down waste. The rate of accumulation depends on household size, water use, and what goes down the drain. Keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications -- to keep solids from building up faster than normal.
